headline.purpose: Page titles: device list heading, device name on the detail page.

title.purpose: Section headers: Alerts, Settings, chart titles.

label.purpose: Gauge instrument labels and device-type chips, uppercase tracked.

numeral.purpose: Live digit at a gauge's center; tabular monospace so updates never jitter in width.

shadows.name: glow-nominal
shadows.purpose: Gauge needle/dial glow when the reading is nominal.

shadows.name: glow-approaching
shadows.purpose: Gauge needle/dial glow when the reading is nearing a threshold.

shadows.name: glow-breached
shadows.purpose: Gauge needle/dial glow when the reading is out of range or has an open alert — measurably brighter, the alert-brightness raise.

shadows.name: alert-dot-halo
shadows.purpose: Small status-dot glow on an unacknowledged alert in the alert list.

motion.name: needle-ease
motion.purpose: Gauge needle rotation on value update — the one authored moment every gauge shares.

motion.name: dim-transition
motion.purpose: Focus-dim: neighboring tiles fade to 50% opacity when one tile is hovered or focused.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Gauge SVG fades to 40% opacity when a device goes offline.

components.name: Gauge (signature)
components.description: The radial instrument every surface composes: 240 degree dial, eased needle, tabular numeral, state-driven glow.
components.html: 21.2°CTEMP
components.css: .ds-gauge { position: relative; width: 112px; height: 112px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-gauge-svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; transition: opacity 500ms; } .ds-gauge-needle { transform-origin: 100px 94px; filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px #dd9834); } .ds-gauge-hub { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 3px #dd9834); } .ds-gauge-readout { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; top: 66%; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; text-align: center; pointer-events: none; } .ds-gauge-numeral { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; font-size: 1.125rem; color: #d9cbb0; } .ds-gauge-label { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; color: #9c8a6e; } .ds-gauge-sublabel { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #9c8a6e; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid amber action button; the one primary action per view (Claim device, Create device).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #a8631c; color: #fff; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; border: none; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #c97f22; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #dd9834; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Ghost/bordered button for Cancel, Add manually, and settings actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #d9cbb0; padding: 6px 12px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid #453829; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #262019; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #dd9834; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card / Tile
components.description: Flat 1px-bordered panel; base container for device tiles, forms, and detail sections.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #1c1712; border: 1px solid #332a20; border-radius: 8px; padding: 16px; color: #d9cbb0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text field used across device-add and settings forms.
components.css: .ds-input { background: #14110e; color: #d9cbb0; border: 1px solid #453829; border-radius: 6px; padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #dd9834; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Device-Type Chip
components.description: Category badge distinguishing a Temp + Gravity module from a Hub; not a status indicator.
components.css: .ds-chip { background: #262019; color: #dd9834; border-radius: 6px; padding: 2px 6px; font-size: 0.625rem; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; }

components.name: Tab Navigation
components.description: Flat row of uppercase tab buttons sharing one bottom border; active tab gets brew-400 text plus a 2px brew-400 underline, inactive tabs are panel-400 hovering to panel-200. Used on the device settings page to split Profile/Setup/Tools/Data.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 4px; border-bottom: 1px solid #332a20; } .ds-tab { padding: 8px 16px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: #9c8a6e; background: transparent; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 0.15s; } .ds-tab:hover { color: #d9cbb0; } .ds-tab-active { color: #dd9834; border-bottom-color: #dd9834; }

narrative.overview:
The dashboard reads like a real gauge cluster mounted over the fermenter, not a status page pretending to be one. Every device is a radial instrument with a needle, a tick-marked dial, and a tabular numeral at its center -- never a card holding a bare number and a colored badge. The ground is a warm charcoal (never pure black) so the panel has a material temperature, and the one recurring accent -- amber phosphor glow -- lights up nominal readings the way an analog gauge's face would, then shifts to orange and red as a reading approaches or breaches its threshold. This is a code-led build: there was no comp to defer to, so this system is read directly off the shipped dashboard and its two captured viewports, not off intent.

The system stays deliberately quiet everywhere it isn't the gauge. Cards, buttons, and forms are flat 1px-bordered panels with no shadow vocabulary of their own; the only glow in the interface is the state signal on a needle, a dial center, or an unacknowledged alert dot. Nothing decorative competes with that signal.
keyCharacteristics: Warm dark charcoal panel ground, never cold or pure black
One state vocabulary -- nominal / approaching / breached / offline -- expressed as glow color and glow intensity, reused identically everywhere a reading appears
Tabular monospace numerals on every live digit; uppercase tracked labels beneath them
Flat, unshadowed containers; glow is a state signal, not ambient depth
Focus-dim: bringing one instrument forward dims its neighbors instead of a badge or modal calling it out

rules.name: The Glow-Carries-State Rule
rules.body: A gauge's state is never color alone. Nominal, approaching, breached, and offline each pair a hue with a distinct glow radius (3px / 5px / 9px / none) so severity reads as intensity before hue even registers -- the alert-brightness raise. Don't reintroduce state as a separate badge or icon once a gauge already carries it.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: `brew` is the only accent hue in the system outside the state vocabulary. It is not spent on decoration -- only on the nominal glow and on primary actions.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerals Rule
rules.body: Every live-updating digit -- gauge readouts, alert temperatures -- uses the monospace stack with tabular-nums. This is a legibility mechanism, not a technical costume, so it is never applied to static or non-numeric text.

rules.name: The Flat-Except-Lit Rule
rules.body: Containers never cast a shadow. The only glow permitted anywhere is the state glow already defined per gauge/indicator -- don't add ambient shadow or glow to a card, button, or chip that isn't reporting a live state.

dos: Do use the four-state vocabulary (nominal/approaching/breached/offline) -- and its paired glow intensity -- for any future live-reading indicator, not just Gauge.
Do keep every live-updating digit in the monospace tabular stack.
Do keep containers flat (1px border, no shadow); reserve glow strictly for state signaling.
Do theme browser-default surfaces (selection, scrollbar, focus ring) from the panel/amber palette rather than leaving them at browser defaults.
donts: Don't add a status badge or icon next to a gauge -- the instrument already carries its own state.
Don't introduce a second accent hue; amber is the only accent outside the state vocabulary.
Don't add shadows, colored side-borders, or gradients to cards, chips, or buttons -- those are not part of this system.
Don't widen the gauge beyond its two sizes (sm/lg) or break its 240 degree dial into a full circle; the speedometer face is the signature silhouette.
